'''Sudha Bhattacharya''' (born 7 March 1952) is an Indian academic, scientist and a writer. She is recognized primarily for her in-depth study of [[Entamoeba histolytica]], a parasitic protozoan that causes [[amoebiasis]]: Dr. Bhattacharya's laboratory first detected [[Ribosomal RNA]] genes on [[Extrachromosomal DNA#Extrachromosomal circular DNA|Circular DNA]], while studying the parasite, and also discovered families of [[retrotransposons]] in the parasite [[genome]].<ref name="insa">{{cite web | url=https://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=P14-1635 | title=INSA profile on Dr. Bhattacharya | accessdate=29 August 2016}}</ref> Her work has primarily been in the fields of Molecular Parasitology and [[Gene regulation|Gene Regulation]].

Bhattacharya is a professor at the School of Environmental Sciences, [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]] (JNU). She is a fellow at [[The National Academy of Sciences, India]],<ref name="Bhattacharya, Prof. Sudha Fellow profile">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Bhattacharya,_Prof._Sudha | title=Bhattacharya, Prof. Sudha Fellow profile | accessdate=15 March 2014}}</ref> [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] and [[Indian National Science Academy]] (2014).<ref name="jnufclty">{{cite web|title=Dr. Bhattacharya's JNU faculty profile|url=http://www.jnu.ac.in/FacultyStaff/ShowProfile.asp?SendUserName=sbhattacharya|access-date=29 August 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118123732/http://www.jnu.ac.in/FacultyStaff/ShowProfile.asp?SendUserName=sbhattacharya|archive-date=18 January 2017}}</ref>

== Education and career==
Sudha Bhattacharya attended [[University of Delhi]] where she graduated with a BSc.(Hons) degree in Botany in the year 1971 and then proceeded to the [[Indian Agricultural Research Institute]], [[New Delhi]] where she obtained her MSc. in Biochemistry and Molecular Biology. She completed her post-graduation in 1973 and then, in 1977, earned a Ph. D. for research on regulation of [[RNA#Synthesis|RNA synthesis]] in [[Escherichia coli]]. She has conducted post-doctoral research on [[bacteriophage]] genetics at [[Stanford University]] (1977–79), [[DNA replication#Bacteria|bacterial DNA replication]] at the [[Boston Biomedical Research Institute]] (1979-1981) and studied [[Axenic|axenic cultivation]] at the [[National Institutes of Health]] (1985–86).<ref name="jnufclty" />

Prior to joining the [[Jawaharlal Nehru University]], Bhattacharya has worked at the [[All India Institute of Medical Sciences]] as a research officer from 1981–82 and at the [[Tata Research Development and Design Centre]] as a [[scientist]] from 1982-85 to research on DNA-based diagnostic methods for common diseases. She joined JNU in 1986 as an [[Assistant professor|Assistant Professor]] and set up her lab to study ''[[E. histolytica]].'' She has also served on the academic committee of various boards affiliated to JNU.<ref name="insa" /> In her attempt towards recognising environmentalists who rely on traditional knowledge, she found [[Jadav Payeng|Jadhav Payeng]] from [[Assam]] who converted 1,00 acres of dense land into a forest for rhinos and elephants.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.terisas.ac.in/index.php?option=com_faculty&task=aboutcv&fid=0483|title=Faculty - Sudha Bhattacharya|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|url-status=|access-date=}}</ref>

== Academic and Research Achievements ==
Dr. Bhattacharya received global acclaim for her novel findings in the field of simple [[molecular biology]] of [[E. histolytica|E. Histolytica]]. Her lab found the existence of [[ribosomal RNA]] genes on round [[DNA]], and located families of [[retrotransposon]]s inside the parasite genome. Study on the replication of [[RDNA (microarchitecture)|rDNA]] established the existence of replication origins inside the rDNA circle, which were differentially used in response to growth strain.  Expression evaluation of rRNA and r-proteins discovered the post-transcriptional regulation of ribosomal [[biogenesis]]. Her work on [[retrotransposon]]s confirmed that retrotransposition is observed by means of excessive frequency recombination- which could contribute to series polymorphism determined in retrotransposons. Her lab also applied the widespread insertion site polymorphism of retrotransposons to broaden a way for pressure typing of E. Histolytica clinical isolates.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.jnu.ac.in/Faculty/sbhattacharya/|title=Prof.Sudha Bhattacharya|website=www.jnu.ac.in|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==

*[[World Bank scholarship|Robert McNamara Fellowship]], [[World Bank]] (1985)<ref name="jnufclty" />
*[[Rockefeller Foundation|Rockefeller]] Biotechnology Career Development Award (1987)<ref name="jnufclty" />
*[[John E. Fogarty International Center|Fogarty International]] Research Collaboration Award (1996 and 2001)<ref name="jnufclty" />
* Fellow of [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (2001), [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] (2008) and [[Indian National Science Academy]] (2014)<ref name="jnufclty" />
*[http://www.serb.gov.in/jcbn.php J.C. Bose National Fellow] (2015)<ref name="insa" />
*Member of the [[Guha Research Conference]] (1993)<ref name="insa" />

== Other contributions ==
Dr. Bhattacharya has served in the Academic Committees of various JNU-affiliated Institutes such as CDRI, ICGEB to name few. She served as Dean, School of Environmental Sciences (2010–12) and played a major role in the all-round improvement of the academic programme. She has been a sectional committee member of the Animal and Plant Science committee of Indian Academy of Sciences, Bangalore and is currently nominated to its Council. She is member Sectional Committee X of INSA; member Research committee, Animal Sciences & Biotechnology, CSIR; member, Animal Science Program Advisory Committee, SERB; member Governing body of SN Bose National Center of Basic Science, Kolkata; member Scientific Advisory committee, Institute of Pathology, New Delhi; member Editorial Board of J. Bioscience.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/P14-1635|title=INSA :: Indian Fellow Detail|website=insaindia.res.in|access-date=2019-12-08}}</ref>
